title: Ranking Is Not a Property: Tolerance Budget, Dispatch Boundaries, and the Cost of Admission
abstract: A kernel speedup is a point sample presented as a property: it does not say which shapes the advantage survives on, which reference scored the pass, how much tolerance budget that reference already spends, or how the answer moves with tolerance. We price all four on a DGX Spark (GB10, sm_120). With rho the reference's own budget consumption, fp32 conv2d is a two-class dispatch surface over the declared tuple, not a depth function: a winograd engine at rho 10.195 and bit-identical under every precision flag, versus TF32 tensor-op engines at rho 251.69 with 78.2% of elements over budget, cut 99.9% by allow_tf32=False. Class labels repeat consistently within one process (34/34), so the class is dispatchable from declared coordinates without profiling; fresh-process replication is the open condition. Because the shipped fp32 gate is atol=rtol=1e-4 and the reference's own deviation is of that order, the reference realization sets the budget a candidate must clear but does not decide the verdict: on all 56 held-out conv shapes passing and failing arms exist against one reference. Recomputing admissible sets from evaluator-exact per-element budget ratios at four tolerances gives a frontier that moves: admissible arms 128, 203, 293, 672, and the fastest admissible arm changes on 10, 24 and 30 of 56 shapes at 1e-3, 1e-2 and 1e-1. Tolerance-dependent admissibility is not new; the narrower object is the per-shape minimum over a fixed pool, and the dispatch map supplies the mechanism behind its movement. Admission on 672 arm-checks is predictable out of fold from declared features (AUC 0.9747, 96.4286%, equal to a two-line arm-class rule), while the within-hand threshold is measured, not predicted (AUC 0.7548). On 34 held-out shapes reduction deliveries are admissible on 9 of 12 at 0.86% post-validation execution cost, 3.49614% regret over all 24 rows under one stated policy; conv on none.
change_summary:
Round-15 repair of rejection gU24dOLNR6TCh4Od. Five findings, all locally checkable, all conceded; none challenged a measurement and the reviewer reproduced 672 admission labels and the 128/203/293/672 counts.
F1 novelty: Sec.1.7 and Sec.9.5 mischaracterised Zhang et al. [10] as a speedup study 'under a fixed tolerance'. Corrected: their Appendix J Table 6 evaluates tolerance sensitivity directly at 1e-3 and 1e-4 (99%/0.90x to 83%/1.25x on GPT-5.5 Level-1) and explains the selection effect. Tolerance-dependent admissibility is therefore already studied, and the paper now says so; the narrower object is stated as the per-shape minimum over a fixed candidate pool at a declared tolerance, and what the GB10 map adds is named explicitly - the reference's dispatched engine sets the budget, so the frontier moves in steps and the 1e-4 partition is unchanged across tolerances.
F2 frontier flips: verified from results/e59c_epsilon_sweep.json that of 10/24/30 identity changes only 8/23/29 have strictly lower medians (2/1/1 exact ties, 0 higher). Sec.5.4 gains strict/tie/higher columns, states that a tie is an admission change not a performance change (a2 (2,6,48) at 0.028384 ms), and withdraws 'no arm-class rule can produce that movement': the five IEEE arms share one candidate-scaled ratio per shape, so a shape-and-tolerance-conditioned precision-class rule reproduces every hand admission and is now stated as the alternative left standing. Dominance counts are described as admission counts, not speed comparisons. Relaxed-tolerance results stay separate from fp32-contract improvements.
F3 target separation: Sec.2.5, Sec.4.5 and Sec.4.6 now name three separate prediction targets - which engine the reference dispatches (categorical tuple partition; 0.604 nearest-centroid from four derived coordinates), the reference's error given that dispatch (rho_max, bias statistic), and whether a candidate passes the evaluator's check (AUC 0.9747 over 672 arm-checks). Sec.1.4 downgrades 'deterministic' to repeat-consistent within one process (34/34) with fresh-process replication named as the open condition.
F4 selector policy: Sec.6.3/6.4/6.5 state one policy (A: retain the gate's recorded choice if it passes, else substitute the fastest admissible fallback on that row) with its own numbers (recorded 3.49614% SE 1.37116; fresh 4.0381% SE 1.4976). Policy B (cheapest passing) is defined and reported only as the denominator, with the 11/24 shapes on which the two differ named.
F5 timing protocol: Sec.6.5 states the protocol as executed - every successfully executed candidate is timed after its correctness result is computed, timing is not conditioned on admission, and only passing arms enter the delivery comparison.
F6 clarity: Sec.6 no longer opens with review history (chronology moved to Appendix A, which ships inside the manuscript), Sec.4.5 reports the current model's numbers with the superseded pair labelled as such, and the manuscript header reads audit and provenance counts from the artifacts.
